text:
kevin_ops: Heads-up — the daily FinOps dashboard shows a 22% uplift in GPU on-demand spend for eu-west-1 last night. I think it's due to reservation aliasing between projects.

lina_finops: ugh. can you paste the query or dashboard panel? I want to see per-sku breakdown (A100-v4 vs A100-v5).

kevin_ops: here's the query I'm using (bigquery):

```
SELECT sku, sum(cost) as cost, sum(hours) as hours, project_alias
FROM `billing.gcp_usage`\nWHERE region = 'europe-west1' AND usage_start BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
GROUP BY sku, project_alias
ORDER BY cost DESC
```

sam_engineering: the reserved capacity we bought uses alias "redwood-dedicated-eu" but some clusters are launching instances under aliases "infra-eu-spot-fallback" which map to on-demand SKUs. Might be a tagging/mapping bug in the provisioning lambda.

zara_prod_analyst: I can see a jump in model-route cost for reranker-route-embedder — correlates with those nodes. Screenshot from the per-route panel: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/fgT2/finops?panelId=12

lina_finops: is the uplift mostly due to instance-hours or premium network egress? breakdown pls.

kevin_ops: primarily instance-hours. net egress + storage negligible. The SKU mismatch causes reserved capacity not to apply (different committed SKU), so we're billed on-demand.

ops-bot: [deploy] provisioning-lambda v2.3.7 deployed to eu-west-1 at 2026-02-14T23:05:00Z :white_check_mark:

sam_engineering: this explains it — v2.3.7 changed default alias mapping to support new spot pool. Looks like it set alias to "infra-eu-spot-fallback" for preemptible pools and forgot to include the reserved alias mapping. I'll open a quick PR to map both aliases to the reserved SKU.

lina_finops: quick ask: can you add a retroactive attribution in the dashboard so we can split last 48h cost between reserved vs orphaned on-demand? we need this for the quarterly commit reconciliation.

kevin_ops: yes — we can approximate by joining instance metadata with reservation_attached flag from our metastore. Example join:

```
SELECT i.instance_id, i.sku, b.cost, m.reservation_attached
FROM `billing.instances` b
LEFT JOIN `compute.instances` i USING(instance_id)
LEFT JOIN `metastore.instance_tags` m USING(instance_id)
WHERE region = 'europe-west1' AND usage_start >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 2 DAY)
```

zara_prod_analyst: note that older instances created before Dec 2025 didn't have reservation_attached tag consistently. we'll need a fallback heuristic (match by launch_time and machine_type).

sam_engineering: I'll push a small patch to the metastore writer that backfills reservation_attached for recent instances (48h window) today. Should be low risk.

kevin_ops: timeline? finance wants an updated burn number for the exec sync at 11:30 UTC.

sam_engineering: give me 45m to backfill and update dashboards.

lina_finops: that's tight but fine. If not ready, we'll mark the delta as provisional and include an explanation. Also flag: consider buying a small commitment top-up for eu-west-1 for next 30d while we untangle aliases — cheaper than continued on-demand. I'll run a cost/benefit quick calc.

ops-bot: [alert] reservation-usage anomaly detected: eu-west-1 orphan_rate = 18% (threshold 5%) at 2026-02-14T23:12:10Z :rotating_light:

zara_prod_analyst: adding notes to the dashboard panel explaining the aliasing risk and the planned fix (PR #489).

kevin_ops: PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/provisioning/pull/489 — includes mapping and a small unit test. Deploying to staging now.

sam_engineering: staging logs show reservations applied correctly for new launches. I'll schedule a canary deploy to production targeting low-traffic pools first.

lina_finops: thanks team. after the patch and backfill let's compare actuals and run a simulated commitment delta: 30d top-up vs projected orphan spend. If orphan spend > 40% of top-up, approve purchase.

kevin_ops: noted. I'll post final numbers once backfill completes. :thumbsup:

zara_prod_analyst: final note — set an alert for orphan_rate > 8% during rollouts so we don't hit this unnoticed again.

ops-bot: [task] create alert rule orphan_rate_threshold_eu = 8% created by ops-bot at 2026-02-14T23:18:55Z

kevin_ops: closing the loop — backfill completed at 23:29 UTC, updated dashboard, provisional delta reduced from $11.2k to $2.1k for the 48h window. PR canary going fine.

lina_finops: excellent. include the $2.1k residual in tonight's burnnote and tag it as "orphaned reservation mismatch (patched)".

sam_engineering: rolling out full deploy now, monitoring.

kevin_ops: thanks all, follow-up tomorrow for the 30d commitment decision.
